legend: Cytospin of pleural fluid (Wright–Giemsa stain) from a patient with an anterior mediastinal mass and pleural effusion shows medium-sized to large mononuclear cells with irregular nuclei, fine to condensed chromatin, small to indistinct nucleoli, moderate cytoplasm, and cytoplasmic vacuoles (findings more typical of transformed mature lymphocytes). Flow cytometry shows that these are T-cell lymphoblasts. Bone marrow involvement is not known at this time point.

Mediastinal mass core needle biopsy shows sheets of medium-sized mononuclear cells with fine chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, nuclear convolutions, and scant cytoplasm. Accompanying bone marrow aspirate smears were negative.
Paraffin immunohistochemistry shows that the tumour cells are CD1a+. They are also CD3+, TdT+ (subset), and CD34− (not shown).

diagnosis: Minimal residual disease of T-lymphoblastic leukaemia
legend: No blasts were morphologically identified on a bone marrow aspirate smear in a patient with T-lymphoblastic leukaemia at day 15 of induction chemotherapy. However, flow-based minimal residual disease analysis of 750 000 events shows 1.36% T-cell lymphoblasts (red population) that are positive for both cCD3 (gate P4) and CD34 (gate P7). Normal bone marrow aspirates do not have T-cell lymphoblasts.
